questions.prompt: What dominates the run time of a GPU radix sort?
options: Memory traffic: how many times keys cross DRAM
questions.explanation: It's memory-bound, so key movements set the time.

questions.prompt: Why can all digit histograms be computed in one upfront pass?
options: Digits are independent of the order keys end up in, so each key contributes to every digit position's histogram at once
questions.explanation: The counts of each digit value don't depend on earlier passes, only on the keys.

questions.prompt: For 32-bit keys with 8-bit digits, how many key movements per key does Onesweep need in total (upfront histogram read + 2 per pass)?
How does a tile learn how many keys of each digit come from earlier tiles, within one pass?
options: Decoupled look-back over per-digit tile counts
It waits for all tiles to finish
questions.explanation: The same X/A/P look-back as single-pass scan, now per digit.

questions.prompt: What general lesson does Onesweep share with kernel fusion and FlashAttention?
options: Remove passes over data: compute what you need up front and cooperate within one pass
questions.explanation: Fewer passes over memory is the theme of memory-bound optimisation.
